articles.headline: Next.js 15 patches critical ImageResponse vulnerability
articles.dek: Next.js releases a security update that hardens the ImageResponse API on both edge and Node runtimes; builders should apply it now.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Next.js 15 includes a security hardening that closes a critical upstream flaw in the ImageResponse implementation used by edge and Node servers [FACT:991c0b80751e3c2848c7df5fa04acee4][FACT:31f30e0ce2f13a8754bfd51c0197bc26]. The bug allowed improperly escaped SVG payloads to bypass sanit‑checks, potentially leading to XSS on pages that render dynamic images [FACT:2707b61c7f965a873c373fd6a39d3649].
Why This Matters

Platform teams that serve images from Next.js edge functions or Node servers risk serving malicious SVGs if they stay on a pre‑15 version [FACT:7104ad89fc8f1945125f59c38f936ec6][FACT:38c3d645799d23493fb41fa61ba257fc]. The vulnerability is upstream, so it affects any project that pulls the default "next" package from npm.
What Happened

The Next.js team announced the patch on Sep 22, 2026 and flagged it as a critical security update [FACT:991c0b80751e3c2848c7df5fa04acee4][FACT:849cdbf662394dd7021dfe66fbf9376d]. The fix lives in version 15 and upgrades several upstream dependencies to safe versions [FACT:d764d00111edf546c040ea22e65008be].
Builder View

If your CI pipeline installs "next" via npm, bump to 15 with a simple "npm install next@15" and redeploy [FACT:96f0da671f10c59ca2d547300bdf90c0][FACT:6c29038a2093bfd46ecac11872e65c96]. The change is pure JavaScript; no config switches are required, but you should verify that any custom ImageResponse handling still works after the upgrade.
Open Questions

The blog notes that the patch does not affect performance, but real‑world load testing is still pending. Vercel’s security program has not yet published a public CVE identifier, so tracking that ID may be useful for compliance reporting [FACT:f7fc00d7592649c3a3791f388339839c].
Ardur Take

Two independent sources confirm the update, and the upstream fix is already packaged in the released version [FACT:991c0b80751e3c2848c7df5fa04acee4][FACT:31f30e0ce2f13a8754bfd51c0197bc26]. Treat this as a mandatory bump for any production Next.js deployment.

keyPoints: Next.js 15 patches a critical ImageResponse vulnerability that could allow unsafe SVG injection [FACT:2707b61c7f965a873c373fd6a39d3649]
Both edge and Node runtimes are affected, so any deployment using "next" needs the update [FACT:7104ad89fc8f1945125f59c38f936ec6][FACT:38c3d645799d23493fb41fa61ba257fc]
Upgrade is a single npm command; no code changes required [FACT:96f0da671f10c59ca2d547300bdf90c0]
